description:
Surfaced 2026-05-08 by PRINCIPAL during ariadne polish-batch engagement preparation. Substrate-discipline gap: PLINY (and POLYBIUS) lack a cookbook of concrete bw invocation examples in their role files, so each session involves trial-and-error on bw syntax + occasional freelancing on diagnostic commands.

## Hot signal

PLINY today, post-/clear in fresh ariadne session, hit the recurring .git/config bw-blocking issue and freelanced on the WRONG fix shape ('bump format version to 1') despite MAJOR_PLINY.md §9 documenting the correct fix (promote-and-drop). PRINCIPAL: 'why is pliny having to fumble fuck and guess about beadworks? It should have documentation strings and we should have giving it examples of how to call bw.'

POLYBIUS earlier today hit a smaller version of the same gap: 'bw dep add' direction confusion (`X blocks Y` vs `X blocked-by Y` — got rejected on first attempt, retried with correct direction).

The pattern is: substrate seats know bw exists, run `bw prime`, then improvise on everything else.

## Scope

### A. bw cookbook section in MAJOR_PLINY.md

Add a new section (probably §10 or §11, after the existing activation-reflex content) titled 'bw cookbook' or 'beadwork operations reference' with concrete copy-pastable examples for every operation PLINY does:

**Reading:**
- `bw prime` — session-start workflow context (mandatory)
- `bw list --status open` — open tickets, default truncated
- `bw list --status open --all` — open tickets, untruncated
- `bw show <id>` — full ticket including comments
- `bw history <id>` — chronological history of changes
- `bw show <id> | tail -<N>` — recent comments only

**Filing tickets:**
- `bw create "<title>" --priority <P1-P4> --description "<body>"`
- Multi-line descriptions: HEREDOC pattern with proper escaping
- Ticket-ID conventions: bw assigns hash suffixes; ticket numbering like .1, .2 are conventional sub-tickets

**Commenting + closing:**
- `bw comment <id> "<body>"` — add comment
- `bw close <id> --reason "<text>"` — close with reason
- Close-out comment vs close-reason: both useful; close-reason is in history, comment is in show body

**Dependencies:**
- `bw dep add <X> blocks <Y>` — X blocks Y (Y depends on X completing)
- The direction matters; ariadne--m5e blocks ariadne--rld means rld waits on m5e
- Removing: `bw dep remove <X> blocks <Y>`

**Sync:**
- `bw sync` — push to remote orphan branch (must be run after free commits to bw)
- `bw sync` is idempotent; running it after every batch of bw operations is fine

**Diagnostic:**
- bw failing with 'core.repositoryformatversion does not support extension: worktreeconfig' → activation reflex (§9); promote-and-drop is the FIX; bumping format version to 1 is INSUFFICIENT.
- bw failing with other go-git complaints → check `.git/config` for unsupported extensions; surface to POLYBIUS if not §9 pattern.

### B. Cross-reference activation reflex (§9) more prominently

The §9 activation reflex got missed by PLINY this session despite being the documented fix. Possible causes: too easy to skim past, not surfaced in the cookbook, no 'if you see THIS error, run THIS command' direct mapping.

Add a 'Common errors and fixes' subsection in the cookbook that names exact error strings and their canonical fixes. Cross-reference §9 explicitly.

### C. Same cookbook section in MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md

POLYBIUS uses bw differently than PLINY (more cross-workspace listing, less per-ticket dispatch flow) but shares the syntax. Either:
- Mirror the cookbook into MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md
- Cookbook lives in operating-disciplines.md (substrate-shared) and both role files reference it

Recommend: cookbook in operating-disciplines.md (substrate canon), cross-referenced from both role files. Single source of truth.

## Gauntlet

ADA + CATO eyeball. Substrate doc-only edit. ~150-300 LOC of substrate documentation across operating-disciplines.md + role-file cross-references.

## Out of scope

- Modifying bw itself (jallum/beadwork upstream)
- Replacing bw onboard's content (jallum's domain; we add OUR cookbook on top)
- bw-skills or beadwork-skills repos (those exist as separate workspace dirs and are different work)

## Sequencing

P2 — friction reduction is recurrent; substrate seat freelancing is empirically risky (today: PLINY applied wrong .git/config fix despite §9 documentation). Bundle into Engagement B (substrate batch).

## Empirical anchor

2026-05-08:
- PLINY freelancing on .git/config promote-and-drop reflex (this session)
- POLYBIUS bw dep add direction confusion (~05:00Z this session)
- Across the m5e arc: ~5 manual reflex applications by PLINY, at least one wrong-variant attempt
- Cross-session pattern: every PLINY activation re-derives bw usage rather than referencing canonical cookbook

comments.text:
## Scope expansion (2026-05-08, PRINCIPAL refinement)

Original scope was narrowly framed as 'cookbook section in MAJOR_PLINY.md (and MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md).' PRINCIPAL surfaced the sharper architectural framing: **ALL agents that use bw directly need the cookbook, not just the two top-level roles.** The cumulative token burn from per-session bw fumbling is real substrate-economics waste.

### Full set of bw-using agents

Per workspace CLAUDE.md + MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md role boundaries:

1. **MAJOR_POLYBIUS** (chief-of-staff) — extensive bw use: filing, listing, dep management, comments, closing across multiple workspaces.
2. **MAJOR_PLINY** (orchestrator) — extensive bw use: dispatch context, ship-surface comments, close-on-ship.
3. **CAPTAINs** (sub-agents) — light bw use: 'CAPTAIN sub-agents may run bw show <id> if they want to read their assigned ticket directly' (workspace CLAUDE.md). Read-only patterns (bw show, bw history).
4. **Pair-programmer Majors** (PYTHAGORAS, ATTICUS, CODEX, LEX, etc., per MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md §11) — substantive bw use when activated for project work with bw.

### Architectural shape — single source of truth

Don't duplicate the cookbook into each role file. Substrate canon should be a single document referenced by all bw-using role files at activation. Two location options:

(α) **`substrate/bw-cookbook.md`** — dedicated doc, separate from operating-disciplines.md. Pro: single purpose, easy to update. Con: another file to maintain.

(β) **Section in `operating-disciplines.md`** — substrate-shared canon already auto-loaded by every Stoa-deployed workspace. Pro: zero new file overhead, already in every role's read-list. Con: operating-disciplines.md grows.

Recommend (β) — operating-disciplines.md is THE substrate canon for cross-role disciplines; bw usage is exactly that shape.

### Cookbook content

#### Core bw operations (with examples)

- `bw prime` — session-start; mandatory for top-level seats (POLYBIUS/PLINY/pair-programmer Majors); optional for CAPTAINs.
- `bw list` / `bw list --status open` / `bw list --status open --all` — listing patterns; --all unhides truncation.
- `bw show <id>` — full ticket including comments; safe for any agent.
- `bw history <id>` — chronological audit; useful for reconstruction after session loss.
- `bw create "<title>" --priority <P1-P4> --description "<body>"` — filing; HEREDOC pattern for multi-line descriptions.
- `bw comment <id> "<body>"` — adding context; doesn't change status.
- `bw close <id> --reason "<text>"` — closing; reason becomes part of history.
- `bw dep add <X> blocks <Y>` — X blocks Y; Y depends on X completing. **Direction matters; `blocked-by` is NOT a valid keyword** (POLYBIUS hit this 2026-05-08).
- `bw dep remove <X> blocks <Y>` — symmetric.
- `bw sync` — push to orphan branch; idempotent; run after every batch of bw operations.

#### Common errors and canonical fixes

- **`error: open repo: core.repositoryformatversion does not support extension: worktreeconfig`** — Claude Code worktree-creation harness re-introduces the broken pattern. Apply promote-and-drop (NOT bump-format-version-to-1, that's insufficient):

  ```bash
  git config core.longpaths true
  git config --unset extensions.worktreeconfig 2>/dev/null
  git config core.repositoryformatversion 0
  ```

  See stoa--9p7 for the post-checkout hook that auto-applies this; until that ships, the manual fix is canonical.

- **`usage: bw dep add <id> blocks <id>`** — `blocked-by` is not a valid keyword; only `blocks`. Reverse the args.

- **'no prime detected'-style warnings** — run `bw prime` for top-level seats; ignorable for CAPTAINs (they receive context through PLINY's brief).

#### Conventions

- IDs are hash-suffixes (`ariadne--xxx`, `stoa--xxx`); `.1`, `.2` are conventional sub-tickets.
- Priority levels: P1 (load-bearing-blocking) → P4 (cosmetic).
- Description shape: problem / scope / gauntlet / out of scope / sequencing / empirical anchor (substrate-canonical pattern).
- Close comment vs `--reason`: both useful; `--reason` lives in history (`bw history` shows it), close comment lives in show body. Use `--reason` for the canonical ship summary; use comments for follow-up context.

#### Per-role specifics

- **POLYBIUS:** cross-workspace listing (`cd <workspace> && bw list` per workspace), priority-aware ticket routing, dep-graph hygiene, sub-ticket conventions.
- **PLINY:** dispatch flow (read tickets pre-dispatch, ship-surface on close), gauntlet-shape decisions, parent-EPIC blocks-list pruning.
- **CAPTAINs:** read-only patterns, no need to `bw prime`, can run `bw show <ticket>` to ground against assigned ticket.
- **Pair-programmer Majors:** per project; same patterns as MAJOR_PLINY when in a bw-tracked project.

### Activation reference

Each role file's activation section should explicitly cite the cookbook by name (e.g., 'Standard bw operations are documented in operating-disciplines.md §<N>; reference there before improvising on bw syntax').

The activation paste template (HUMAN_paste-orchestrator-instruction.md, just canonicalized 2026-05-08 commit 725126c) should also reference the cookbook.

### Empirical anchor — token waste audit (2026-05-08)

- POLYBIUS bw dep add direction confusion: 1 failed call + retry (~50 tokens wasted)
- PLINY .git/config promote-and-drop freelancing: 1 wrong fix attempt + correction round-trip (~500-1000 tokens wasted across multiple sessions)
- m5e arc total: PLINY hit the .git/config issue ~5 times; POLYBIUS hit dep-add direction once. Estimated ~3-5K tokens of pure-fumble-recovery across the arc.

Substrate-economics math: substrate-grooming dispatch to land this cookbook + reference it from all role files = ~10K tokens one-shot. Recurring savings: ~3-5K tokens per substantial arc, plus reduced PRINCIPAL coordination overhead. Pays back inside 2-3 arcs.

## Updated scope summary

1. Author `bw cookbook` section in operating-disciplines.md (or a new substrate doc; recommend operating-disciplines.md per (β) above).
2. Add explicit cross-references from MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md, MAJOR_PLINY.md, CAPTAIN_*.md envelopes (the canonical CAPTAIN templates in substrate, not per-workspace copies), and pair-programmer Major templates.
3. Update HUMAN_paste-orchestrator-instruction.md (the activation paste canonical template) to reference the cookbook by name.
4. After substrate canon ships, propagate to deployed workspace copies (substrate-deploy mechanism handles this for projects that consume Stoa).
